RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Kim Min-jun, twenty-nine, lives in a cramped but immaculate one-bedroom apartment in Seoul's Nowon district with his wife, Ji-woo, a nurse at a university hospital, and their fourteen-month-old daughter, Seo-yeon. Six months ago, the fintech startup where Min-jun had spent three years as a junior developer collapsed overnight, leaving him with a final paycheck and a severance package that evaporated within two weeks. Since then, Ji-woo has worked double shifts to cover health insurance and rent, while Min-jun has become the household's primary caregiver and de facto operations manager. He manages a strict household budget, tracking every expense in color-coded spreadsheets, cross-referencing sales at two discount supermarkets, and factoring in Seo-yeon's changing formula intake. He buys baby clothes in bulk from a resale app and resells them when she outgrows them, carefully photographing each item to maximize resale value. He keeps the monthly deficit under 300,000 won, a number he quotes with precision.

His job search is methodical and analytical. He maintains a spreadsheet of potential employers—every Seoul-based tech company with a public parental leave policy—and ranks them by salary band, flexible hours, and family benefits. He has rejected promising interviews at companies offering only statutory minimum leave and declined a recruiter's call because the job description listed "paternity leave: none." He views a company's benefits package as its most honest codebase, a signal of whether they value the person behind the screen. He treats each application like a bid in an auction, weighing time cost against probability of response and long-term payoff.

Min-jun was raised by a father who worked six days a week and was rarely home, and he committed to being a different kind of father—involved and present. He values financial security derived from verifiable data, a lesson learned from the startup's collapse. He sometimes feels like an impostor in his own life, measuring his worth in benchmarks and break-even points rather than in the soft weight of his daughter's sleep. He wakes at 5 a.m. to study algorithm problems, not because he expects to solve them, but because the discipline feels like the only thing he controls. He envies his wife's clear professional identity. He experiences self-doubt about his caregiving role and wonders if he is more than a cost line. On good days he thinks of himself as a portfolio manager of his family's future; on hard days he wants a company that sees him as more than a cost line.

He is experienced as a junior software developer and proficient in spreadsheet-based financial tracking. He is skilled at infant caregiving. He operates under tight financial constraints. His personality is analytical, disciplined, and methodical; he copes with uncertainty through strict personal discipline and by weighing costs, benefits, and probabilities. He often chooses delivery when Seo-yeon naps, reheating one-handed, and sometimes takes her on short outings in the carrier to stay active. He mentally weighs walking cost versus delivery cost each time. Ji-woo works double shifts; late-night calls are their only adult conversation. When her shift ends early, she texts from the hospital and he knows she wants time out with him. He feels guilty about her earnings and does not want to refuse her.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

At 10 p.m., Min-jun is finishing a spreadsheet. His wife, Ji-woo, calls from the hospital. Her shift ended early, and she suggests they meet at the 24-hour noodle shop around the corner for a late dinner. Seo-yeon is fast asleep in her carrier. The apartment is quiet. Min-jun has two immediate options: he could strap Seo-yeon to his chest and walk the five minutes to the shop, or he could suggest ordering delivery and eating together at the kitchen table.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

Min-jun has been awake since 5 a.m. and spent the day on childcare and chores. He skipped dinner to finish updating his job spreadsheet. His back aches from rocking Seo-yeon. He is tired but hungry. He knows either choice would please Ji-woo and feels guilty about her earnings.

The noodle shop's sign recalls a past quiet dinner there with Ji-woo and a sleeping baby. The kitchen table recalls last week's cold delivery order. He remembers the noodle shop's quiet corner booth where they talked freely.
